3D Print Farm

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In an exclusive we show how the 3d printing community have mobilized to assist hospitals in preparing for the influx of Covid-19 infected patients.

Unique Selling Point:
It started two weeks ago when Bernhard Vogt of AMS 3d printers thought if Italian and American doctors can do it, why can't we. Together with other 3d printing companies, and even clients who had bought 1 or two printers he created a whatsapp group which I've been a part of from the beginning. The group called "3d print farm" - began to mobilize anyone from the 3d printing community who wanted to begin practicing through trial and error designs already made available from other countries who were already in the midst of thousands of corona virus infected patients. From watching youtube videos: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ItpExBEieY&feature=youtu.be and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pP7z3iw76GA - the trial and error of printing these designs began. Please see pics i've uploaded to this link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1-DH3iowLJEmAOqdf8KGCJPgQXE1zZ1je

https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/simplae-face-shield-frame-rsa
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4225667

From fask masks, protective gear and even ventilator components... the group tried everything out there and were in constant communication. They rallied each other, and shared their successes and failures, taking photo's of settings and examples that worked... tirelessly for the past week, then they had the designs ready, but no where to put them?

Summary:
Then yesterday 27 March the first Corona death was announced and this spurred the group into more action - they got a hold of netcare911 whose ambulance drivers were looking to partner with 3d printers, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1APqsTqUWrfr1fiIGOFxhZdtYe_sIsXPG?fbclid=IwAR3E0HiqRHmk8wpz9fW8Y_gRjdCgH3g2YKocpMSKZYOm0MGKWONyTU6MP7A (offical netcare letter)

But now emergency services - Joburg CBD emergency services - collected from marius, doctor in khalafong (50 units) and department of health (5 in midrand), netcare911 (kevin) are all asking for the masks! So we have a few nice case studies - like a doctor in a government hospital etc. there are various different types of face shields and masks - I have filmed some of them and have seen them being printed. I am in touch with numerous people about getting information.

And as they had already mobilized and were already clued up with the approved international designs -the department of health are testing right now. The 3D PRINT FARM already have made 1000s of shields and face masks. And whose paying for this? It's for FREE - the 3D printing community had one goal, if they all help out and share the cost (which is cheap a couple of rands worth of product per print) they were all happy to come together to chip in. There are lots of very nice angles in this. The hospital are happy to speak, the 3d printing community have been filming their efforts for me... and collecting the products using ambulances.

Further information:
We will film this will cellphones, whatsapp, presenter links and can film in person some parts. I've got 3-4 3d printing characters - bernhard, michael scholtz(who has 1 printer he bought) and is really taken over the running of the group - please see the spread sheet they made of how many printers each of them has and who is already printing units: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1o4CxEzFAia4sCtS92_-10eb0uyb1TZf2E1AZpcog7os/edit#gid=0

*the group has grown from 20 to almost 100 in the past 24 hours.
Bernhard also says hes getting calls from companies pledging materials and money to assist in buying more - everything is volunteered.

this is the design netcare has them printing:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hI7c-rGawOmeadCR8fd4VNenaaSDUxVh

eVEN SCHOOL CHILDREN HAVE JOINED: https://www.facebook.com/163205890550124/posts/1262693840601318/?vh=e&d=n
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1APqsTqUWrfr1fiIGOFxhZdtYe_sIsXPG?fbclid=IwAR3E0HiqRHmk8wpz9fW8Y_gRjdCgH3g2YKocpMSKZYOm0MGKWONyTU6MP7A

Michael Scholtz has made this video explainer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI0thsQFybo

People like cornelius just bought a 3d printer for fun - like to print things for their own personal use and now he's contributing positively to help fight the virus. i think a story like this would be great to try and assist people in keeping up their spirits during the lockdown!

Script:


We first met Bernhard Vogt three weeks ago when he revealed how his small 3D printing company was hijacked by the Gupta’s during state capture. Vogt has slowly begun to pick up the pieces, rebuilding his business, but then the Novel coronavirus hit South Africa and the president imposed a 21 day lockdown. As the infection rate started rapidly increasing, and reports emerged of a shortage of masks and protective material Vogt stepped up to the plate to print 3d masks and face shields.
Bernhard: We saw a lot of initiatives in Italy and Spain where 3D printing was done. So we thought about we need to start mobilizing the community early to to start printing and be prepared
Vogt googled designs and started a whatsapp group which combined 3d print stores, and anyone at home with a 3d printer…
Bernhard: in the community. I estimate there is more than a thousand printers probably closer to 2000. So if you're doing the massive if you've got two thousand guys printing 10 a day that's a lot of face masks that can be produced.
THE ADVANTAGES OF 3D PRINTING ARE ACTUALLY PERFECT FOR A LOCK DOWN... IT REQUIRES VERY LITTLE HUMAN INTERACTION AND CAN BE DONE IN THE MANUFACTURER’S HOME ALL WHILE ADHERING TO THE RULES OF STAYING INDOORS WHILE CONTRIBUTING TO PREVENTIVE MEASURES FOR THOSE ON THE FRONTLINE
Bernhard: The first target or people that should be getting them would be your first first responders. We've been told that they have very little protective gear and when they go out to see a patient they can only get a mask if they can verify that this patient is at risk to spread a viral disease.
As the initiative grew nationally, provincial group leaders appeared.
Michael: “ I’d like to tell you about a group printing medical devices for medical professionals during this time of need…”
Michael Scholtz’s day job is fixing computers...
Michael: some people collect handbags, watches,I enjoy collecting tools, (switch)
Another hobby of his? 3D printing MORE 3d printers...
Michael: It ended up building itself really and eventually I had enough decent parts to print parts for a second printer
Masa: Those are the three components right Michael? I’m going to try and figure this out now...[Masa tries putting together mask…]And there we have it, made my first mask!
Michael: We referring to that collective community as a distributed printer farm. It's Essentially a Small factory distributed over thousands of homes in South Africa.
Masa: What would the cost be of something like this?
Michael: probably about 40 to 50 rand's worth of filament.
Bernhard: So what we said from the beginning is that this a community project, okay there should be no profiting from this.
Michael: We are doing this to put these things in the hands of the people who in a week a month three months from now might be the person in the ambulance saving our own lives.
Marius: I've been a firefighter for many years I actually often printed the first one. I was amazed of how good it fits.
Marius Buys is a fireman and has a 3d printer at home, he says the masks fit perfectly and integrate into their equipment - and when used properly don’t fog up their protective glasses.
Marius: You can actually take one out of it. Cut it out in ninety five ask put it inside and you can actually use it in ninety five. About five to six times. We actually tested the points to see if they don't just break easily, and how we actually need to clean it because the protection also for the firefighters and the industry is actually paramount.
Buys got Johannesburg’s emergency services on board
Fireman: we’re happy, because we can only change that filter, and then we can wash it instead of throwing away the whole mask.
Vogt donated 3d printing material to the university of pretoria...Upsound: “ we happy”
....as well as to the paramedics from the Community Emergency Response Team SA who are likely to come into contact with potentially infected coronavirus patients.
guy 2: These are the 3d masks and those are the face shields...
Dr Carlos Hartmann, a gynaecologist at a Durban private hospital also started using a face shield.
Hartman: This shield is a magnificent way to protect your face so
its as simple as having the software of a 3d printer, I got the frame and the mask yesterday and i used it while doing a cesarean section we always have a little splash of blood, but it definitely protects you.
The speed with which one of these masks sets are made is roughly around six to seven hours.
The face shields that we can three print do still take around an hour to print the frame. There are other designs coming out that are ingenious. A laser cutter can make a shield out of a free sheet of acetate In under two minutes. That is a huge increase.
We can 3d print a splitter units which will allow one ventilator to service more than one patient at a time so you can hook up for patients to one machine.
IT IS GREAT THAT THERE ARE HUNDREDS OF THESE MINI AT HOME 3D PRINTING FACTORIES, BUT THIS DOES NEED TO BE REGULATED TO ENSURE A HIGH MANUFACTURING STANDARD. MANY OF THOSE WHO ARE PART OF THIS COMMUNITY ARE CALLING FOR THIS AND WELCOME ANY FORMALIZED GOVERNMENT REGULATION.
As materials dwindle during the lockdown, the 3d print farm community will try their best to meet the demand.
Bernhard: Steve Biko phoned me this morning they'd be 4000 face to face shields
Michael: There's a limited supply of filament, so we need to practice a bit of restraint. I think the biggest benefit of the way that this is distributed is. Let's say I get sick I'm one little node in a thousand Factories so it becomes a self sustaining Organism.
Bernhard: This is a time for for us as people of South Africa to pull together every guy that can do to pull his weight and not to ask us for oh can you give us materials. Can you pay my time. Can you pay my electricity.That's your small contribution to the cause.

So we have a few nice case studies - like a doctor in a government hospital etc. there are various different types of face shields and masks - I have filmed some of them and have seen them being printed. I am in touch with numerous people about getting information. And as they had already mobilized and were already clued up with the approved international designs -the department of health are testing right now. The 3D PRINT FARM already have made 1000s of shields and face masks. And whose paying for this? It's for FREE - the 3D printing community had one goal, if they all help out and share the cost (which is cheap a couple of rands worth of product per print) they were all happy to come together to chip in. There are lots of very nice angles in this. The hospital are happy to speak, the 3d printing community have been filming their efforts for me... and collecting the products using ambulances.
metadata.Further information: We will film this will cellphones, whatsapp, presenter links and can film in person some parts. I've got 3-4 3d printing characters - bernhard, michael scholtz(who has 1 printer he bought) and is really taken over the running of the group - please see the spread sheet they made of how many printers each of them has and who is already printing units: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1o4CxEzFAia4sCtS92_-10eb0uyb1TZf2E1AZpcog7os/edit#gid=0 *the group has grown from 20 to almost 100 in the past 24 hours. Bernhard also says hes getting calls from companies pledging materials and money to assist in buying more - everything is volunteered. this is the design netcare has them printing: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hI7c-rGawOmeadCR8fd4VNenaaSDUxVh eVEN SCHOOL CHILDREN HAVE JOINED: https://www.facebook.com/163205890550124/posts/1262693840601318/?vh=e&d=n https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1APqsTqUWrfr1fiIGOFxhZdtYe_sIsXPG?fbclid=IwAR3E0HiqRHmk8wpz9fW8Y_gRjdCgH3g2YKocpMSKZYOm0MGKWONyTU6MP7A Michael Scholtz has made this video explainer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI0thsQFybo People like cornelius just bought a 3d printer for fun - like to print things for their own personal use and now he's contributing positively to help fight the virus. i think a story like this would be great to try and assist people in keeping up their spirits during the lockdown!
